full_judgment: 11. The learned Advocate also submits that none of the independent and disinterested witness of the case was examined in this case, and there is no explanation from the side of the prosecution as to the non- production of the witnesses in and around the place of occurrence and as such the convict-appellant is entitled to get the benefit of section 114(g) of the Evidence Act, wherein it has been emphasized that failure to examine disinterested witnesses makes the prosecution case shaky, in the same way as being held in the case of The State Vs. Basirullah reported in 16 DLR 189 and that non-examination of relevant witnesses creates presumption under the said section and raises a question of doubt in the prosecution and benefit of this defence would go to the accused. She further submits that there are gross contradictions and discrepancies in the evidence of prosecution witnesses and as such the evidence of the prosecution witnesses are unworthy of credit and that the prosecution could not establish the case beyond all reasonable doubt.
